nodes.summary: Degnan & Rosenberg (2006), eq. (4): the boundary `a(x)` of the four-species anomaly zone, for a deeper internal branch of length `x > 0` (at `x = 0` the denominator vanishes and Lean's `a / 0 = 0` gives the junk value `log (2/3 - 0)`; `a(x) → ∞` as `x → 0⁺`).
nodes.title: Boundary of the four-species anomaly zone

nodes.summary: `b` is maximal at `0`: `b(x) ≤ log (7/6)` for `x ≥ 0`, so for `y ≥ log (7/6)` at most one gene tree is anomalous.
nodes.title: Three-anomaly boundary is maximal at zero

nodes.summary: `b(0) = log (7/6)` (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006): if `y ≥ log (7/6)`, then `y ≥ b(x)` for every `x ≥ 0` (`anomalyB_le_anomalyB_zero`).
nodes.title: Value $\log(7/6)$ of the three-anomaly boundary at zero

nodes.summary: Degnan & Rosenberg (2006), eq. (5): the boundary `b(x)` below which the caterpillar species tree has three anomalous gene trees (defined for `x ≥ 0`).
nodes.title: Boundary for three anomalous gene trees

nodes.summary: No anomalous gene trees on the balanced four-species tree (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006): for nonnegative branch lengths, no gene tree is more probable than the one matching the species tree `((0, 1), (2, 3))`. Given the numbers of lineages entering the root population, the matching tree is already the most probable outcome of random joining.
nodes.title: No anomalous gene trees on the balanced four-species tree

nodes.summary: The symmetric gene tree `((a, b), (c, d))` on four genes, as a set of clusters.
nodes.title: Balanced four-gene tree

nodes.summary: The symmetric (balanced) species tree `((0, 1), (2, 3))` with internal branch lengths `y₁` (above the ancestor of `0, 1`) and `y₂` (above the ancestor of `2, 3`).
nodes.title: Balanced four-species tree

nodes.summary: One population of the multispecies coalescent along a branch of length `t`. It receives `m` lineages `bs` (and the clusters `acc` formed below it). Under Kingman's coalescent the number `j` of lineages left at the top of the branch has law `tavareProb m j t` (Tavaré's formula, `exp_blockCountingGenerator_apply`), and, independently of the coalescence times, the order of the `m - j` coalescences is the beginning of…
nodes.title: Coalescence along one branch of the species tree

nodes.summary: On the caterpillar species tree with `x ≥ 0`, the gene trees `((A, C), (B, D))` and `((A, D), (B, C))` are more probable than the matching gene tree if and only if `y < b(x)`.
nodes.title: Anomaly of ((A, C), (B, D)) and ((A, D), (B, C)) on the caterpillar

nodes.summary: Anomalous gene tree on four species (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006): on the caterpillar species tree with deeper branch `x > 0` and shallower branch `y`, the symmetric gene tree `((A, B), (C, D))` is more probable than the gene tree matching the species tree if and only if `y < a(x)`. With `caterpillar_le_matching` this gives `caterpillar_exists_anomalous_iff`.
nodes.title: Anomalous gene tree on four species

nodes.summary: The four-species anomaly zone (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006, Definition 1 and Figure 2): the caterpillar species tree with deeper branch `x > 0` and shallower branch `y ≥ 0` has an anomalous gene tree, one strictly more probable than the gene tree matching the species tree, if and only if `y < a(x)`.
nodes.title: The four-species anomaly zone

nodes.summary: On the caterpillar species tree with nonnegative branch lengths, no asymmetric gene tree is more probable than the matching one (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006): only the three balanced gene trees can be anomalous.
nodes.title: Only balanced gene trees can be anomalous on the caterpillar

nodes.summary: The asymmetric gene tree `(((a, b), c), d)` on four genes, as a set of clusters.
nodes.title: Caterpillar four-gene tree

nodes.summary: The asymmetric (caterpillar) species tree `(((0, 1), 2), 3)`: `x` is the length of the deeper internal branch (above the ancestor of `0, 1, 2`) and `y` that of the shallower one (above the ancestor of `0, 1`), as in Degnan & Rosenberg (2006).
nodes.title: Caterpillar four-species tree

nodes.summary: The clusters formed during the first `t` coalescence events of `h` from the lineages `bs`: every lineage present at some step `u ≤ t`, as the set of sampled genes it is ancestral to.
nodes.title: Clusters formed along a ranked history

nodes.summary: The species tree `(((0, 1), 2), 3)` has the clusters of the gene tree `(((0, 1), 2), 3)`.
nodes.title: Clusters of the caterpillar species tree

nodes.summary: The species tree `((0, 1), 2)` has the clusters of the gene tree with cherry `{0, 1}`.
nodes.title: Clusters of the three-species tree

nodes.summary: The clusters (clades) of a species tree: the sets of species below its vertices, including the singletons and the full set of species.
nodes.title: Clusters of a species tree

nodes.summary: A rooted gene tree on four genes `G` (a set of clusters) displays the quartet split `ab | cd`, where `{c, d}` is the complement of `{a, b}`: forgetting the root, the internal edge separates `{a, b}` from `{c, d}`; equivalently `{a, b}` or `{c, d}` is a cluster.
nodes.title: Gene tree displaying a quartet split

nodes.summary: Degnan & Rosenberg (2006): for `x ≥ 0`, the gene tree `((A, C), (B, D))` (equivalently `((A, D), (B, C))`) is more probable than the matching gene tree, `f(x, y) < g(x, y)`, if and only if `y < b(x)`.
nodes.title: Degnan–Rosenberg criterion: $f(x, y) < g(x, y)$ iff $y < b(x)$

nodes.summary: The boundary `a(x)` of the anomaly zone (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006): for a deeper internal branch `x > 0`, the symmetric gene tree `((A, B), (C, D))` is more probable than the matching gene tree, `f(x, y) < h(x, y)`, if and only if `y < a(x)`.
nodes.title: The boundary `a(x)` of the anomaly zone

nodes.summary: Degnan & Rosenberg (2006), eq. (1): `f(x, y)`, the probability of the matching gene tree `(((A, B), C), D)` on the caterpillar species tree.
nodes.title: Degnan–Rosenberg probability of the matching caterpillar gene tree

nodes.summary: `g(x, y) ≤ h(x, y)` for a nonnegative shallower branch (equality at `y = 0`).
nodes.title: $g(x, y) \le h(x, y)$ for a nonnegative shallower branch

nodes.summary: For a positive shallower branch, the symmetric gene tree `((A, B), (C, D))` is strictly more probable than `((A, C), (B, D))`: `g(x, y) < h(x, y)` (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006).
nodes.title: $g(x, y) < h(x, y)$ for a positive shallower branch

nodes.summary: Degnan & Rosenberg (2006), eq. (2): `g(x, y)`, the probability of the gene tree `((A, C), (B, D))` (and of `((A, D), (B, C))`) on the caterpillar species tree.
nodes.title: Degnan–Rosenberg formula g for the gene tree ((A, C), (B, D))

nodes.summary: Degnan & Rosenberg (2006), eq. (3): `h(x, y)`, the probability of the gene tree `((A, B), (C, D))` on the caterpillar species tree.
nodes.title: Degnan–Rosenberg formula h for the gene tree ((A, B), (C, D))

nodes.summary: `exitLaw` is additive in the continuation.
nodes.title: Additivity of the exit law

nodes.summary: If a continuation takes the constant value `c` whenever at least one lineage exits, then so does `exitLaw` (Tavaré's probabilities sum to one and random joining is a probability).
nodes.title: Exit law of a constant continuation

nodes.summary: On a species tree with nonnegative branch lengths, `exitLaw` of a continuation that is nonnegative whenever at least one lineage exits is nonnegative (Tavaré's probabilities are nonnegative, `tavareProb_nonneg`).
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the exit law

nodes.summary: The law of the lineages leaving the top of the branch above a vertex of the species tree, in continuation-passing form: `exitLaw T k` is the expectation of `k m bs acc`, where `m` is the number of exiting lineages, `bs` the lineages and `acc` the clusters formed below. The two daughter populations evolve independently, and their lineages enter the ancestral population together.
nodes.title: Law of the lineages leaving a species-tree branch

nodes.summary: No anomalous unrooted quartets, balanced species tree (Allman, Degnan & Rhodes 2011): on `((0, 1), (2, 3))` the unrooted gene quartet matches `01 | 23` with probability `1 - (2/3) e^{-(y₁ + y₂)}`, where `y₁ + y₂` is the internal edge of the unrooted species quartet.
nodes.title: No anomalous unrooted quartets, balanced species tree

nodes.summary: On the balanced species tree the discordant unrooted gene quartet `02 | 13` has probability `(1/3) e^{-(y₁ + y₂)}`.
nodes.title: Probability of quartet split 02|13 on the balanced tree

nodes.summary: On the balanced species tree the discordant unrooted gene quartet `03 | 12` has probability `(1/3) e^{-(y₁ + y₂)}`.
nodes.title: Probability of quartet split 03|12 on the balanced tree

nodes.summary: The symmetric gene tree `((A, B), (C, D))` on the caterpillar species tree has probability `h(x, y)` (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006, eq. (3)).
nodes.title: Probability of the gene tree ((A, B), (C, D)) on the caterpillar

nodes.summary: The symmetric gene tree `((A, C), (B, D))` on the caterpillar species tree has probability `g(x, y)` (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006, eq. (2)).
nodes.title: Probability of the gene tree ((A, C), (B, D)) on the caterpillar

nodes.summary: The symmetric gene tree `((A, D), (B, C))` on the caterpillar species tree has probability `g(x, y)`, the same as `((A, C), (B, D))` (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006).
nodes.title: Probability of the gene tree ((A, D), (B, C)) on the caterpillar

nodes.summary: The matching gene tree on the caterpillar species tree has probability `f(x, y)` (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006, eq. (1)). An identity for all real `x, y`.
nodes.title: The matching gene tree

nodes.summary: No anomalous unrooted quartets, caterpillar species tree (Allman, Degnan & Rhodes 2011): the unrooted gene quartet matches the species quartet `01 | 23` with probability `1 - (2/3) e^{-y}`, where `y` is the length of the internal edge of the unrooted species quartet (the shallower internal branch).
nodes.title: No anomalous unrooted quartets, caterpillar species tree

nodes.summary: On the caterpillar species tree the discordant unrooted gene quartet `02 | 13` has probability `(1/3) e^{-y}`.
nodes.title: Probability of quartet split 02|13 on the caterpillar tree

nodes.summary: On the caterpillar species tree the discordant unrooted gene quartet `03 | 12` has probability `(1/3) e^{-y}`.
nodes.title: Probability of quartet split 03|12 on the caterpillar tree

nodes.summary: An event containing every gene tree has weight one, for every species tree.
nodes.title: Total gene-tree probability is one

nodes.summary: On a species tree with nonnegative branch lengths, every gene-tree probability is at most one.
nodes.title: Gene-tree probabilities are at most one

nodes.summary: The branch length stored at the root of a species tree does not affect the gene tree.
nodes.title: Root branch length does not affect gene-tree probabilities

nodes.summary: Gene-tree probabilities are nonnegative on species trees with nonnegative branch lengths. (For a negative branch length they need not be.)
nodes.title: Gene-tree probabilities are nonnegative

nodes.summary: The probabilities of two disjoint events of gene trees add up. With `geneTreeProb_nonneg` and `geneTreeProb_true`, `geneTreeProb T` is a probability law when `T.NonnegLengths`.
nodes.title: Additivity

nodes.summary: Each discordant three-species gene tree has probability `(1/3) e^{-t}`: cherry `{0, 2}`.
nodes.title: Probability of the discordant three-species gene tree with cherry {0, 2}

nodes.summary: Each discordant three-species gene tree has probability `(1/3) e^{-t}`: cherry `{1, 2}`.
nodes.title: Probability of the discordant three-species gene tree with cherry {1, 2}

nodes.summary: Three-species concordance (Hudson 1983; Pamilo & Nei 1988): with one lineage per species and internal branch length `t`, the gene tree matches the species tree with probability `1 - (2/3) e^{-t}`. (An identity for every real `t`; branch lengths are `t ≥ 0`.)
nodes.title: Three-species concordance

nodes.summary: For every species tree, the event "any gene tree" has weight one (an identity for every real branch length). With `geneTreeProb_nonneg` and `geneTreeProb_or` this makes `geneTreeProb T` a probability law when `T.NonnegLengths`.
nodes.title: Normalization

nodes.summary: The multispecies coalescent (Pamilo & Nei 1988; Degnan & Salter 2005), one lineage sampled per species: the probability that the gene tree, given by its set of clusters, lies in the event `E`. Below the root, each branch population runs Kingman's coalescent for the branch length (`branchStep`); in the root population all remaining lineages coalesce by random joining. The definition accepts any real branch lengths;…
nodes.title: The multispecies coalescent

nodes.summary: `integral_randomJoining` for a rational-valued function, with a rational result (used to evaluate random-joining probabilities by computation).
nodes.title: Rational-valued expectation under random joining

nodes.summary: An expectation under random joining is the average over the `∏_{k=2}^m C(k, 2)` ranked histories.
nodes.title: Expectation under random joining as an average over histories

nodes.summary: `G` is one of the three balanced (symmetric) gene trees on four genes.
nodes.title: Balanced gene tree on four genes

nodes.summary: The set `S` of sampled genes is a clade of the ranked history `h`: it is a block of one of the ancestral partitions of `h`, i.e. the set of descendants of some lineage.
nodes.title: Clade of a ranked history

nodes.summary: Starting from the singletons, `mergeAlong` is `blocksAfter`.
nodes.title: Merging lineages from singletons gives the ancestral blocks

nodes.summary: The lineages after the first `t` coalescence events of the ranked history `h` (of `m` lineages), starting from the lineages `bs`, each given as the set of sampled genes it is ancestral to. Events follow the encoding of `RankedHistory`: the pair `{a, b}` with `a < b` merges into position `a`, and position `b` is removed (`mergeBlocks`). With the singletons as starting lineages this is `blocksAfter`…
nodes.title: Lineages after the first coalescence events of a ranked history

nodes.summary: Every branch length of the species tree, including the unused one stored at the root, is nonnegative. On such trees `geneTreeProb` is a probability law; for a negative length it is only a signed weight.
nodes.title: Species tree with nonnegative branch lengths

nodes.summary: The case `m ≤ 5` of `randomJoining_isClade`.
nodes.title: Clade probability under random joining for at most five genes

nodes.summary: Clade probability (Rosenberg 2003): under random joining, a fixed set of `k` among `m` genes, `1 ≤ k < m`, is a clade with probability `2m / (k (k + 1) C(m, k))`.
nodes.title: Clade probability

nodes.summary: The probability of an event under random joining is the fraction of ranked histories in it.
nodes.title: Random-joining probability as a fraction of ranked histories

nodes.summary: The topology of a species tree, forgetting branch lengths, as a planar rooted binary tree.
nodes.title: Topology of a species tree

nodes.summary: A rooted binary species tree on the species `Fin n` with branch lengths: `leaf i` is species `i`, and `node l r t` is the ancestral species of the species below `l` and `r`, where `t` is the length, in coalescent units (`2N` generations), of the branch above the node, i.e. the time during which the ancestral population of `l` and `r` exists before it merges with a sister population. The length stored at the root…
nodes.title: Rooted binary species tree with branch lengths

nodes.summary: The species quartet maximizes quartet support (Allman, Degnan & Rhodes 2011; Mirarab et al. 2014): for a positive internal edge, the unrooted gene quartet matching the species quartet is strictly the most probable of the three, on both four-species shapes. Since the expected quartet support of a candidate four-species tree (one quartet) is the probability of its quartet, the species tree maximizes it.
nodes.title: The species quartet maximizes quartet support

nodes.summary: From `m ≥ 1` lineages, the number of ancestors at time `t` is one of `1, …, m`. (The rows of `exp (t • G)` restricted to the states `≥ 1` sum to one because `G` kills the indicator of `{1, …, n}`; an identity for every real `t`.)
nodes.title: Tavaré's probabilities sum to one

nodes.summary: Tavaré's probabilities are nonnegative for `t ≥ 0`: `exp (t • G)` is the entrywise limit of powers of the Wright–Fisher transition matrix (`tendsto_wfLineageMatrix_pow_floor`), whose entries are nonnegative. (For `t < 0` they can be negative or exceed one.)
nodes.title: Tavaré's probabilities are nonnegative

nodes.summary: Three lineages have one ancestor at time `t` with probability `1 - (3/2) e^{-t} + (1/2) e^{-3t}`.
nodes.title: Three lineages have one ancestor at time $t$

nodes.summary: Three lineages are still distinct after time `t` with probability `e^{-3t}`.
nodes.title: Three lineages remain distinct with probability $e^{-3t}$

nodes.summary: Three lineages have two ancestors at time `t` with probability `(3/2)(e^{-t} - e^{-3t})`.
nodes.title: Three lineages have two ancestors at time $t$

nodes.summary: Two lineages have coalesced within time `t` with probability `1 - e^{-t}`.
nodes.title: Two lineages coalesce with probability $1 - e^{-t}$

nodes.summary: Two lineages are still distinct after time `t` with probability `e^{-t}`.
nodes.title: Two lineages remain distinct with probability $e^{-t}$

nodes.summary: The species below a node.
nodes.title: Species below a node of a species tree

nodes.summary: `a(x) → ∞` as `x → 0⁺` (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006): very short deep branches produce an anomalous gene tree however long the shallower branch is.
nodes.title: Anomaly-zone boundary blows up for short deep branches

nodes.summary: The three-species probabilities come from the Wright–Fisher model: in a population of `M` gene copies, the lineages of species `0` and `1` have distinct parents in each of the `⌊t M⌋` generations of the internal branch (`t ≥ 0` coalescent units) with probability `noCoalProb M 2 ^ ⌊t M⌋`, which tends to `tavareProb 2 2 t = e^{-t}`, the weight of the case in which three lineages reach the root population.
nodes.title: Wright–Fisher limit of the no-coalescence probability

nodes.summary: No anomalous gene trees for three species (Degnan & Rosenberg 2006): for a positive internal branch, each discordant gene tree is strictly less probable than the matching one.
nodes.title: No anomalous gene trees for three species

nodes.summary: The gene tree on three genes with cherry `c` (a pair of genes), as a set of clusters.
nodes.title: Three-gene tree with a given cherry

nodes.summary: The three-species tree `((0, 1), 2)` with internal branch length `t`.
nodes.title: Three-species tree ((0, 1), 2)
Mathematical Biology

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
